SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

AARON EDWARD HOWTON'S PLEADING IN SUPPORT OF KEVIN KENNEDY AND JOHN BURROWS' REQUEST FOR INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION AND FORENSIC AUDIT
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Intervenor Aaron Edward Howton, appearing pro se, respectfully files this pleading in support of the request by Kevin Kennedy and John Burrows for an independent investigation and forensic audit in PUC Docket No. 59475, identified by Mr. Howton as PUC Interchange Item No. 6571. Mr. Howton supports that request because the Commission's remand places reliability need and claimed consumer congestion-cost savings squarely at issue, and those questions depend on forecasts, models, source data, cost assumptions, planning judgments, and procedural records that should be capable of independent verification.
Mr. Howton does not ask the Administrative Law Judges to presume fraud, misconduct, or any other violation before the evidence is examined. The purpose of an independent investigation and forensic audit is the opposite: to determine, through a neutral review of native records and underlying data, what occurred, what assumptions were used, whether material information was accurate and complete, and whether the conclusions presented to the Commission can be independently reproduced and validated.
I.  STATEMENT OF SUPPORT
Mr. Howton supports the Kennedy-Burrows request because an independent review would strengthen the integrity of the administrative record and public confidence in any final decision. This proceeding concerns an unprecedented 765-kV transmission project with substantial consequences for ratepayers, landowners, communities, and the use of private property. When a decision of that magnitude rests materially on technical forecasts and planning analyses generated by interested or participating institutions, independent verification is a reasonable safeguard.
Mr. Howton's own remand filing already asks that the record distinguish between three different things: an ERCOT forecast or model result; an Applicant's reliance on that forecast or model result; and actual independent validation of the underlying data, assumptions, methodology, and conclusions. Those are not the same thing. ERCOT's technical role is important, but ERCOT cannot serve as the independent validator of its own planning work.
II.  THE EXISTING RECORD PROVIDES A REASONABLE BASIS FOR INDEPENDENT REVIEW
The hearing record demonstrates why independent verification is appropriate. During the hearing on the merits, testimony established that ERCOT performed the principal reliability studies underlying the project and that key figures concerning import-path options, transfer capability, and losses were taken from ERCOT's study. The record also reflects that no ERCOT witness was present to testify to that work during the cited examination. See Hearing on the Merits Transcript, Vol. 4, at 48-49.
The record also contains disputes concerning the accuracy and timing of information used in the routing and notice process. Mr. Kennedy's cross-examination, for example, questioned whether then-current Bell County tax records reflected a subdivision that had been platted before notice data were pulled. See Hearing on the Merits Transcript, Vol. 4, at 18-19. That exchange does not by itself establish intentional wrongdoing, but it illustrates why a neutral review of source records, dates, data pulls, revisions, and decision logs could materially assist the Commission.
Mr. Howton's evidence and filings have likewise raised concerns about the reliability of desktop and aerial data, habitable-structure counts, cultural and historical resources, environmental information, route changes, and the timing and adequacy of notice to later-affected landowners. The proper response to contested data is not to assume either side is correct. It is to test the data against the original records and determine what can be verified.
III.  THE COMMISSION REMAND MAKES INDEPENDENT VALIDATION ESPECIALLY RELEVANT
The Commission's September 11, 2026 remand requires further consideration of Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13, including whether the proposed facilities are necessary to meet applicable reliability standards and whether estimated congestion-cost savings for consumers may result. Those questions cannot be answered confidently if the material inputs, assumptions, model versions, forecast vintages, or cost calculations cannot be independently reproduced.
PURA § 39.151(d) makes an ERCOT independent organization directly responsible and accountable to the Commission and authorizes meaningful Commission oversight of ERCOT's finances, budget, and operations. Mr. Howton therefore supports a review that tests, rather than merely summarizes, the ERCOT-derived work product relied upon in this case. To the extent a full forensic audit requires authority or resources beyond SOAH's role in this contested case, that limitation is a reason to refer or recommend the request to the Commission or other legally authorized oversight body—not a reason to leave material questions unexamined.
IV.  SCOPE OF THE REQUESTED INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION AND FORENSIC AUDIT
At a minimum, Mr. Howton respectfully submits that an independent review should examine the following subjects:
1.  Planning chronology and decision-making. The chronology of the decision to pursue 765-kV facilities; the dates on which material alternatives were evaluated or eliminated; communications among ERCOT, the Applicants, consultants, and other participating entities; and the basis for major planning decisions.
2.  Forecasts, models, and underlying data. The ERCOT load forecasts, large-load assumptions, generation assumptions, retirements, storage, renewable and gas-generation assumptions, model versions, contingency criteria, transmission constraints, voltage and thermal limits, and sensitivity analyses used to conclude that the project is necessary.
3.  Alternatives analysis. Whether lower-voltage configurations, staged construction, additional generation, storage, demand response, HVDC or other transmission configurations, and other reasonable alternatives were evaluated using comparable assumptions and objective criteria.
4.  Cost, procurement, and ratepayer exposure. The capital-cost assumptions, congestion-savings calculations, expected utilization, long-lead equipment commitments, procurement timing, material financial commitments made before final CCN approval, and the allocation of financial risk and benefits to ratepayers and participating entities.
5.  Routing, notice, and data integrity. The source and date of landowner records; material route additions or changes; habitable-structure data; environmental, cultural, historical, and community-resource information; corrections or errata; and whether affected landowners received notice based on accurate and current information.
6.  Independence and conflicts. The identity and role of entities that prepared, reviewed, approved, or financially benefited from the studies and recommendations, and whether any truly independent engineering or financial validation was performed before the project was presented for approval.
7.  Record preservation and reproducibility. Preservation and review of native electronic records, including relevant emails, spreadsheets, model inputs and outputs, study files, data extracts, change logs, contracts, and other records needed to reproduce material conclusions and determine when information was created, changed, or relied upon.
V.  THE REVIEW SHOULD BE INDEPENDENT, DOCUMENTED, AND TRANSPARENT
For the review to have value, the reviewer should be independent of ERCOT, the Applicants, and any transmission provider or consultant with a material financial interest in the 765-kV buildout. The reviewer should have appropriate engineering, utility-planning, data-forensics, and financial expertise and should be given access to native source materials sufficient to test the material assumptions and calculations.
The resulting report should identify the materials reviewed, the methodology used, any limitations on access, any assumptions that could not be reproduced, any material discrepancies discovered, and whether the reliability-need and congestion-savings conclusions can be independently validated. Legitimately confidential information can be protected through the Commission's existing procedures without preventing meaningful independent review or public findings.
VI.  SUPPORT FOR RELIEF WITHIN THE TRIBUNAL'S LAWFUL AUTHORITY
Mr. Howton recognizes that SOAH's authority on remand is defined by the Commission's order and that certain investigative or audit powers may belong to the Commission, the Legislature, the State Auditor, or another authorized entity. His support for the Kennedy-Burrows request is therefore directed to relief that is lawful in the appropriate forum.
Within this proceeding, Mr. Howton respectfully asks the ALJs to preserve the issue, recognize its direct relationship to the remanded reliability and consumer-benefit questions, require the parties to identify any independent validation already performed, and make clear in any supplemental or amended Proposal for Decision whether the material ERCOT-derived assumptions have or have not been independently validated. If the requested forensic audit cannot be ordered directly by SOAH, Mr. Howton asks that the request be transmitted, referred, or expressly recommended for consideration by the Commission or other body possessing the necessary authority.
VII.  PRAYER
For these reasons, Aaron Edward Howton respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges accept this pleading as his formal support for Kevin Kennedy and John Burrows' request for an independent investigation and forensic audit; grant or recommend that request to the fullest extent permitted by law; require preservation and identification of the native records and source data necessary for independent review; require disclosure of any prior independent validation of the material ERCOT-derived forecasts, models, cost calculations, and planning assumptions; and ensure that the supplemental or amended Proposal for Decision clearly states what has been independently verified and what remains unverified.
Mr. Howton further requests that no final determination of reliability need or claimed consumer congestion-cost savings be treated as independently established merely because an ERCOT study or Applicant-sponsored filing repeats those conclusions, and that all other relief to which he may be entitled be granted.

Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Aaron Edward Howton
Aaron Edward Howton
Pro Se Intervenor
12600 FM 2843
Salado, Texas 76571
Telephone: 254-291-7888
Email: eddy@enconsulting.us
CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that on September 18, 2026, a true and correct copy of this pleading was served on all parties of record in accordance with the Commission's procedural rules and the applicable orders in this proceeding.
/s/ Aaron Edward Howton

1. Public Utility Commission of Texas, Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH, PUC Docket No. 59475 (Sept. 11, 2026).
2. Public Utility Commission of Texas, Preliminary Order, PUC Docket No. 59475 (Mar. 30, 2026), Issue Nos. 11 and 13.
3. Kevin Kennedy and John Burrows' request for independent investigation and forensic audit, identified by Mr. Howton as PUC Interchange Item No. 6571.
4. Aaron Edward Howton's Motion for Limited Reopening of the Record, Supplemental Briefing, and Independent Validation of ERCOT Reliability and Congestion-Cost Assumptions on Remand (Sept. 18, 2026).
5. PURA § 39.151(d) (Commission oversight and investigatory authority concerning an ERCOT independent organization).
6. Texas Government Code §§ 321.002, 321.013, and 321.0136 (Legislative Audit Committee and State Auditor authorities).
7. Hearing on the Merits Transcript, Vol. 4, PUC Docket No. 59475, including testimony at pages 18-19 and 48-49 concerning notice/tax-record questions and ERCOT-derived reliability-study information.
